question: Should `openclaw/plugin-sdk/archive`, `openclaw/plugin-sdk/root-walk`, and `openclaw/plugin-sdk/secret-file` become supported public Plugin SDK contracts, or should the filesystem helpers remain internal until a narrower API is approved?
rationale: The new subpaths are externally consumable compatibility surfaces; implementation tests cannot determine whether OpenClaw should support, version, and deprecate them as permanent plugin APIs.

options.title: Approve the three public SDK subpaths
options.body: Accept them as supported Plugin SDK contracts and require focused compatibility coverage plus clear ownership documentation.

options.title: Keep the filesystem helpers internal
options.body: Remove the new public exports and retain only private or bundled-plugin seams until a narrower external contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Approve the three public SDK subpaths
recommendation.body: Accept them as supported Plugin SDK contracts and require focused compatibility coverage plus clear ownership documentation.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history ties this person to both the active fs-safe adoption and the closely related merged state-runtime migration, making them the strongest routing candidate in the supplied evidence.
